DTR · TALK ABOUT A SCENE

The Diary Beside the Declaration

STS-HS11-L3-BR300-HSELA1112-HJD-MNA-01 • HS English 11-12 • Foundational U.S. Documents: Themes, Purposes, and Rhetorical Features
Look at the picture. You will answer some questions about it. Press the play button to hear each question. Record your answer for each question. You can listen to your answer and record it again. Click SUBMIT RECORDINGS when you have answered all the questions.
JUST FOR FUN · OPTIONAL
Historical journals let a reader stand inside a moment instead of reading about it. Layla, Tarek, and Rania are pairing invented diary entries from a family who arrived from Beirut and Casablanca with the exact lines those readers met for the first time in English. A diary says I felt. The Declaration says we hold.
Which one persuades a stranger more, and what does each one want from its reader?
Optional. You do not have to record this one.
1
What is Layla doing?
Look at the picture. Say: Layla is ____ at the low table. (writing / eating) Then say: She is doing it to ____. (save the words / hide the words)
2
What is Tarek holding?
Look at the picture. Say: Tarek has a big ____. (scroll / ladder) Then say: He is holding it up to ____. (show it / fold it)
3
What is the teacher doing?
Look at the picture. Say: The teacher is ____ something. (carrying / climbing) Then say: She is doing it to ____. (serve the students / stop the students)
4
What room is this? How do you know?
Look at the picture. Say: This is a ____. (library / kitchen) Then say: I know because of the ____. (books / cars)
5
Tell me about the exhibit wall.
Look at the picture. Say: I see ____ on the wall. (papers / windows) Then say: They are up there to ____. (be read / be thrown away)
6
What is Rania wearing?
Look at the picture. Say: Rania has on a ____. (headscarf / helmet) Then say: She wears it ____. (every day / one time)
Record an answer for each question, then submit.
Content alignment: CCSS.ELA-LITERACY.RI.11-12.9 — Analyze foundational U.S. documents for themes, purposes, and rhetorical features. ELD (Speaking — official ELPAC “Talk About a Scene”): PI.A.1, PII.B.3, PII.B.4, PII.B.5.
